priorIterationResolution.note: REQ-010's introduction of a unique per-clip tracking token, mechanically derived from producer.sh's existing clip_id (verified real at /Users/anicca/anicca/skills/earn/clip/producer.sh:60-62, `${ID}_EN.mp4`), and REQ-008 step 6's redesign to check ONLY for exact token-substring containment (never hook prose), DOES structurally solve the original narrow FIND-025 scenario: traced concretely, two different clips sharing the exact same reused hook text per HARD RULE 0.18 but originating from DIFFERENT source URLs get DIFFERENT clip_ids and therefore different tokens, so hook-text reuse can no longer cause misattribution. PROP-006(b)'s regression test explicitly proves this. HOWEVER the spec's own broader claim that follows from this fix -- 'there is no meaningful residual token-collision risk ... tokens are derived 1:1 from each clip's own unique source-URL-based ID' (behavioral-spec.md, REQ-008 step 6 closing paragraph) -- is FALSE against the real producer.sh code this spec itself cites as ground truth: clip_id is derived from the SOURCE VIDEO URL, not from anything unique to a specific processing run, and producer.sh's default source-selection has no dedup/history check against previously-processed URLs (see FIND-028, new this iteration, critical). The original hook-reuse ambiguity is closed; an isomorphic clip_id-reuse ambiguity has taken its place, unaddressed by the spec.
